review_notes:
I read the whole file with this rubric in mind. I made three searches under Mathlib: for `Memℓp` and `PreLp`, for `ENNReal.HolderConjugate` and `HolderTriple`, and for other ℓp-style spaces. Outside this file, `Memℓp` and `PreLp` appear only in `lpHolder.lean`, `LpEquiv.lean` and one mention in `Kuratowski.lean`, and all of those build on this file. So I found no second independent ℓp definition.

I considered these candidates and rejected them:
- `Memℓp` against `MeasureTheory.MemLp` with counting measure. The representations differ on purpose: the type is dependent, `p = 0` means finite support, and the definition uses summability instead of an integral. They are not the same specific concept under matching assumptions.
- `lp.single`, `lp.singleAddMonoidHom`, `lp.lsingle` against `Pi.single` and `AddMonoidHom.single`. These land in `lp E p`, so they are named specialisations rather than competing definitions.
- `lp.coeFnAddMonoidHom` against `AddSubgroup.subtype`. It is implemented via `AddSubgroup.subtype` and gives a convenient named coercion with its own simp lemma.
- `lp.linearMapOfLE` against `AddSubgroup.inclusion`. The docstring says it is the linear-map version, and `toAddMonoidHom_linearMapOfLE` connects the two.
- `lp.evalₗ` and `lp.evalCLM` against `LinearMap.proj`. The codomain differs, so these are not the same map.
- `lp.zeroBasis` against `Finsupp`. It builds the basis through `Finsupp`.
- `PreLp` against a plain Pi type. It is a documented type synonym that avoids the product topology, with a stated reason.
- `{ i | f i ≠ 0 }` against `Function.support`. This is only notation, not a separate concept.

The Hölder statement `lp.tsum_mul_le_mul_norm` uses real `HolderConjugate`, while `Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean` now has an ENNReal version and the in-file TODO still asks for one. That is a theorem-statement matter, which the rubric excludes. I did not open `lpHolder.lean` to check whether it already covers the case.

I found nothing here that justifies consolidating anything.
